svg.title: NVFP4 versus MXFP4
svg.desc: Two microscaling formats, a teaching dynamic-range example, W4A4, and BitNet.
svg.text: Four bits: value format, scales, and execution path

g.text: a group of 32 E2M1 values × one E8M0 scale
32 values plus a local scale → 4.25 bits/weight
speed requires a compatible hardware kernel
emulation and native execution are different regimes
quality depends on calibration and model sensitivity
a group of 16 × an E4M3 scale + an FP32 scale per tensor
native support in the current NVIDIA documentation: Blackwell
speed depends on the executed hardware kernel
the smaller group tracks local range more closely

svg.text: one outlier-containing vector: uniform INT4 versus an E2M1-like grid
the E2M1-like grid has 3.32× lower MSE here; not a general result
The W4A4 floor: weights AND activations at 4 bits
Cohere reports W4A4 deployment for Command A+ (218B/25B):
one B200 or two H100s; the result belongs to that checkpoint and stack
The choice (Q5): hardware support, scale geometry, calibration, and model-specific quality jointly determine the format
BitNet b1.58: ternary weights require co-designed training, packing, and kernels; a small file does not create fast arithmetic
